title: Overly Generalized Schemas (EAV or JSON Blobs)
pattern: Bypassing strongly typed fields on domain structs or database tables by storing all attributes in a single, generic JSON blob or an Entity-Attribute-Value (EAV) schema to "stay flexible."
why_bad: Shuns compile-time type-safety, pushes validation into fragile, duplicated runtime parsing logic, and severely degrades query performance and index efficiency.
detection: Look for structs where core domain fields are represented by a generic JSON value (`serde_json::Value`) or a flat list of string-keyed maps, rather than typed fields.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Document storage backends, analytics dashboards, or search indexes where raw, arbitrary dynamic schema storage is the primary architectural goal.
fix: Use proper, strongly typed database tables and strongly typed structs for known, invariant domain fields.
source: *Martin Fowler - Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture (2002)*, "Serialized LOB"; *Steve McConnell - Code Complete (2004)*, Chapter 13.
